newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINESE YUAN ENDS UP AT 26-MONTH HIGH VS DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: CHINESE YUAN ENDS UP AT 26-MONTH HIGH VS DOLLAR.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a 26-month high close of 8.2894 on Friday from Thursday's 8.2904 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to heavy buying around the key 8.2900 level, traders said.
The close was the highest since May 18, 1995 when the yuan ended at 8.2892.
Dealers said strong pro-yuan sentiment on the market made many bankers buy the yuan around the 8.2900 level after a fall in the past two days on a technical correction.
"The yuan won firm support today after two days of correction," one dealer said.
A second dealer said reduced intervention by the People's Bank of China boosted buyers' confidence. The bank had intervened to depress the yuan last week.
"If the central bank does not intervene in the next few days, the yuan has potential to go up further," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move just above the 8.2900 level early next week.

On Friday, the yuan opened up at an intraday low of 8.2900 and moved in a small range of 8.2895 and 8.2899 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2861. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2897, traders said.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2903.
The yuan closed little changed at 6.9851 from 6.9850 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0700 from 1.0706 against the Hong Kong dollar.
